result: Fat body depletion causes undisciplined bidirectional migration of tracheal progenitors without affecting their migration rate, cell number, or proliferation. The fat body resides in anatomical proximity to the trachea, and its ablation increases migration entropy.
evaluation: Claims C2, C3, C17-C21 collectively demonstrate that fat body is required for disciplined progenitor migration. The experimental evidence includes imaging (C17, C18, C19), quantitative migration analysis (C19, C20), and entropy measurements (C21), all supported by multiple figures. The controls showing unchanged proliferation and migration rate (C20) strengthen the specificity of the directional phenotype.

result: Fat body-derived Upd2 cytokine induces JAK/STAT signaling in tracheal progenitors to maintain directional migration. Knockdown of upd2 in fat body phenocopies fat body ablation, causing bidirectional progenitor movement.
evaluation: Claims C4, C5, C26-C28 establish the Upd2-JAK/STAT signaling axis. The evidence includes RNAi phenocopy experiments (C26), receptor expression analysis (C27), and ligand-receptor interaction reporter data (C28). The convergence of genetic manipulation and reporter assays provides strong support for this inter-organ signaling mechanism.

result: Perturbation of JAK/STAT signaling components (Dome, Hop, Stat92E) in trachea causes aberrant bidirectional migration of progenitors, leading to incomplete airway regeneration and tracheal melanization.
evaluation: Claims C6, C29-C31 demonstrate that JAK/STAT signaling in trachea is necessary for directional migration. Multiple genetic perturbations (RNAi of dome, hop, stat92E) and pharmacological inhibition (Tofacitinib) all produce consistent bidirectional migration phenotypes (C29, C30), with downstream consequences for tissue integrity (C31). The convergence of multiple approaches strengthens the conclusion.

result: JAK/STAT signaling promotes expression of planar cell polarity genes (ds, fj, ft, fat2, fz, stan, vang) and leads to asymmetric localization of Fat in progenitor cells. ChIP-seq identified 21,312 Stat92E binding peaks, with 95.7% within 2kb of transcription start sites.
evaluation: Claims C7, C8, C32-C34, C81-C83 establish the molecular mechanism linking JAK/STAT to PCP. The ChIP-seq data (C81-C83) provides genome-wide evidence for direct transcriptional regulation, while expression analysis of GFP-tagged reporters (C33, C34) validates specific targets. The asymmetric Fat localization (C8, C39, C40) provides functional evidence for PCP establishment.

result: Perturbation of PCP components (ds, ft, fj) causes bidirectional progenitor migration. Normal progenitors show elevated Ft at the posterior leading edge, while bidirectionally migrating progenitors show Ft at both anterior and posterior edges with filopodia extending from both fronts.
evaluation: Claims C35-C40 demonstrate the functional requirement for PCP components in directional migration. The RNAi experiments (C35) are supported by both loss- and gain-of-function data (C36). The imaging analysis of Ft localization (C39, C40) and filopodia distribution (C37, C38) provides mechanistic insight into how PCP disruption causes bidirectional movement.

result: Upd2 is transported from fat body to tracheal progenitors via vesicles requiring Rab5/Rab7-mediated endocytic sorting, Grasp65-mediated secretion, and Lbm-dependent trafficking. BFA treatment and genetic perturbations sequester Upd2 in fat body and reduce Upd2 puncta in progenitors.
evaluation: Claims C9, C10, C41-C47 establish vesicular transport of Upd2. Multiple lines of evidence converge: pharmacological inhibition (BFA, C41, C43), genetic perturbations (grasp65, lbm, rab5, rab7 RNAi, C44-C46), and imaging of Upd2-mCherry puncta (C42, C43). The control showing tracheal upd2 knockdown has no effect (C47) supports the fat body as the relevant source.

result: Vesicular transport machinery (Grasp65, Lbm, Rab5, Rab7) is essential for JAK/STAT signaling in trachea and directional progenitor migration. Perturbation of vesicle trafficking reduces Stat92E-GFP reporter activity and DIPF ligand-receptor reporter signal, causing bidirectional migration.
evaluation: Claims C48-C56, C76 link vesicular transport to JAK/STAT signaling and migration phenotypes. The evidence includes reporter assays (Stat92E-GFP, DIPF) showing reduced signaling upon perturbation of trafficking components (C48-C53), and migration analysis showing bidirectional movement (C54-C56). The specificity is demonstrated by lack of effect from rab2/rab3 perturbation (C56) and selective effect of BFA on DIPF but not JAK inhibitors (C52, C53).

result: Upd2 physically interacts with Rab5, Rab7, Grasp65, and Lbm in vesicles. Lbm-pHluorin is detected at fat body plasma membrane and in tracheal cells, with signals compromised by Rab5/Rab7 perturbation, indicating Rab-dependent biogenesis of Lbm-containing vesicles that transport Upd2.
evaluation: Claims C57-C65, C77, C78 provide molecular evidence for Upd2-vesicle interactions. Multiple complementary approaches converge: colocalization imaging (C57-C59), proximity ligation assay (C60), co-immunoprecipitation (C61, C62), and functional pHluorin reporter assays (C63-C65). The Rab-dependence of Lbm-pHluorin signals (C65) supports the model that Rab GTPases regulate vesicle biogenesis (C77).

result: RNA-seq of tracheal progenitors from fat body-depleted pupae reveals dramatic transcriptional changes, with enrichment for cytokine activity genes. JAK/STAT, PI3K, and Dpp signaling target genes are upregulated upon progenitor activation but suppressed by fat body depletion.
evaluation: Claims C22-C25 provide transcriptomic evidence for fat body-dependent signaling in progenitors. The RNA-seq analysis (C22) identifies cytokine activity enrichment (C23), and heatmap analysis shows signaling pathway activation (C24) and fat body-dependence (C25). This unbiased approach supports the targeted genetic studies and provides broader context for the Upd2-JAK/STAT mechanism.

result: Background on the tracheal progenitor system: progenitors reside in Tr4/Tr5 metameres, migrate anterior-to-posterior, are activated by Bnl/FGF and insulin, and interact with fat body, which produces regulatory signals affecting other organs.
evaluation: Claims C11-C16 provide established background knowledge supported by citations. These claims set up the biological context for the study but do not represent novel findings. The citations to prior work (Chen and Krasnow 2014, Li et al. 2022, Pitsouli and Perrimon 2010, etc.) appropriately attribute these observations.

result: Discussion and background on JAK/STAT signaling: the pathway does not serve as a guidance cue but directs movement directionality. Background on Upd cytokines, Dome receptor, JAK/STAT mechanism, IL-6 vesicular transport, and tetraspanin function in membrane repair.
evaluation: Claims C66-C75 represent interpretations (C66) and background knowledge (C67-C75) appropriately supported by citations. C66 is a reasonable interpretation of the data showing that JAK/STAT perturbation causes bidirectional rather than random migration. The background claims provide context but are not novel findings.

result: Summary conclusion: tracheal progenitors establish migratory directionality as they exit their niches, and disciplined migration depends on inter-organ signaling from fat body.
evaluation: Claims C79, C80 represent the overall conclusions of the study, synthesizing the experimental findings. These are well-supported by the collective evidence from fat body depletion, Upd2 manipulation, JAK/STAT perturbation, and vesicular transport studies. The claims appropriately summarize the major findings without overstating the conclusions.
